questions.question: Which of the following is the commercial unit of electrical energy?

options.text: Joule
Watt
Kilowatt-hour
Kilowatt

questions.explanation: The commercial unit of electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh), often referred to as a 'unit' in electricity bills. Joule is the SI unit of energy, Watt is the SI unit of power, and Kilowatt is a larger unit of power.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following materials is best suited for making the core of an electromagnet?

options.text: Steel
Copper
Soft iron
Aluminium

questions.explanation: Soft iron is used for the core of an electromagnet because it can be easily magnetized and demagnetized. It has high magnetic permeability and low retentivity, allowing it to acquire strong magnetism when current flows and lose it quickly when the current is switched off.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field lines is INCORRECT?

options.text: They emerge from the North pole and merge into the South pole.
They do not intersect each other.
The density of field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
They form open curves, starting from one pole and ending at the other.

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed loops, extending from the North pole to the South pole outside the magnet, and from the South pole to the North pole inside the magnet. Therefore, they do not form open curves.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: The direction of magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor is determined by:

options.text: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
Maxwell's Right-Hand Thumb Rule
Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction

questions.explanation: Maxwell's Right-Hand Thumb Rule (also known as the Right-Hand Grip Rule) is used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field lines is incorrect?

options.text: They emerge from the North pole and merge into the South pole.
They do not intersect each other.
The density of field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
They form open curves.
options.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed curves, extending from the North pole to the South pole outside the magnet, and from the South pole to the North pole inside the magnet.

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed curves, extending from the North pole to the South pole outside the magnet, and from the South pole to the North pole inside the magnet.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field lines is **incorrect**?

options.text: They are closed curves.
They emerge from the North pole and merge at the South pole outside the magnet.
They intersect each other at points of strong magnetic field.
The density of field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines never intersect each other. If they did, it would mean two directions of magnetic field at the point of intersection, which is not possible.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is primarily used to determine the direction of:

options.text: Induced current in a conductor.
Magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.
Force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.
Electric current in a circuit.

questions.explanation: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule gives the direction of the force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in an external magnetic field, which is the principle behind electric motors.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: What is the primary function of an electric fuse in a household circuit?

options.text: To increase the current in the circuit.
To decrease the voltage in the circuit.
To protect appliances and wiring from excessive current.
To convert AC to DC.

questions.explanation: A fuse is a safety device that melts and breaks the circuit when the current exceeds a safe limit, thus protecting the appliances and wiring from damage due to overloading or short-circuiting.
questions.subject: icse10-physics

questions.question: In a DC generator, the split-ring commutator primarily functions to:

options.text: Provide a path for the magnetic field.
Reverse the direction of current in the external circuit every half rotation.
Generate a stronger magnetic field.
Increase the speed of rotation of the armature.

questions.explanation: The split-ring commutator in a DC generator reverses the direction of current flowing through the external circuit every half rotation
